Architect Server
Network version

Architect Server

Run Architect on one computer and everyone on your network signs in from their browser. It includes local accounts, an admin console, a shared document repository with sharing and version history, and Draw with Claude, which runs in each person's own Claude account. Fully self-contained: it needs no internet connection and no outside accounts or services.

Needs Node.js 18 or newer on the server computer. Works with no internet connection.

Set it up

  1. Install Node.js (LTS) from nodejs.org on the computer that will be the server.
  2. Unzip the-architect-server.zip somewhere permanent, such as C:\TheArchitect.
  3. Start it: double-click start-windows.bat, or run ./start-mac-linux.sh on Mac or Linux.
  4. The window lists the addresses to open and the first admin password. Sign in and choose a new password.
  5. Allow Node.js through the firewall on private networks when Windows asks.
  People open one of these addresses in a web browser:
    http://192.168.1.20:8080      Ethernet
    http://localhost:8080         this computer

  FIRST RUN. Sign in as  admin  with password  k3Jx9pQa2LmT

How people sign in

Where they areWhat they open
On the serverhttp://localhost:8080
Office network or Wi-Fihttp://<server IP>:8080, the address the server window shows
Home or another siteConnect to the company VPN first. Or publish the server over HTTPS with a reverse proxy or secure tunnel (README, section 5).

Everyone signs in with an account on your server: a username and password, optionally with an authenticator-app code, with an Administrator or User role. Administrators add people in Admin console › Users, or let people sign up with approval or an invite code. Anyone given a temporary password chooses their own at first sign-in. If an admin is locked out, run node server.js reset-password admin on the server itself.

Admin console

Open http://server:8080/admin, or use Tools › Admin console. Tabs:

UsersAdd, approve, change role, disable, reset password, delete. A deleted user's diagrams move to you.
DocumentsEvery diagram, with its owner, access and size. Open, share or delete any of them.
SecurityRequired two-step codes from an authenticator app, and whether diagrams can link to spreadsheets at web addresses.
Company libraryUpload icons, logos and shapes everyone sees at the top of the shape library. The section is called Company until you rename it, for example to Cydcor.
SettingsOrganization name, who can create accounts, session length, default sharing, lockout, and limiting the admin console to the local network.
Connected appsOptional. Paste the Client ID and secret of your own Figma app and Canva integration so people can sign in to their own accounts from Architect.
Claude add-inTurn Draw with Claude on or off for everyone, and set the public address used in Claude's links.
ActivitySign-ins, failed sign-ins, sharing changes and admin actions.
ServerListening addresses, uptime, storage, HTTPS status and a backup download.

Draw with Claude

Nothing to configure on the server. Each person clicks Draw with Claude, signs in to their own Claude account, and creates a connection token once. They then describe the diagram, and Claude creates it in their repository. Architect opens it as soon as it appears.

claude mcp add --transport http architect http://server:8080/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

In Claude Desktop, use Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector. For claude.ai, the server must be reachable over HTTPS from the internet.

Figma, Canva and other apps

Sign in from Architect. Once an admin fills in Connected apps, people open File › Connected apps and sign in to their own Figma or Canva account. They can import any Figma file by link, browse their Canva designs and bring them in as editable shapes, and send a diagram to Canva as a new editable design.

Figma plugin. The download includes figma-plugin. In Figma desktop, use Plugins › Development › Import plugin from manifest. Then sign in with your server address and token, and move pages both ways.

Files. Architect opens PowerPoint, Keynote and Google Slides exports, Canva exports, PDF, Illustrator .ai, SVG, Visio, Lucidchart, draw.io, Gliffy, Mermaid and DXF. It saves PowerPoint with editable shapes, vector PDF, SVG, PNG, Visio, draw.io and DXF.
